problem: Integrity's tracked_under dedup (structure-integrity.md ~line 1144) searches OPEN issues only. When a dome-site condition is adjudicated as monitoring-only and its ISS closes, the next integrity re-detection finds no open match, emits tracked_under:null, and decider Step 1d mints a fresh ISS -> full BAU round-trip (decider route -> analyst-baby re-fetch -> reconfirm -> close). This has happened twice for the identical unchanged WIN-062 duplicate-numbering condition: ISS-2961 (2026-07-10 -> closed 07-14 via EXP-661/663) and ISS-3013 (2026-07-25 -> closed 07-27 via EXP-672). Both EXP-663 and EXP-672 investigation notes independently recommended suppression; the recommendation sat unactioned between the two cycles. Cost per recurrence: 1 ISS + 1 tracker item + 1 analyst-baby run + 2 decider touches, all to reconfirm a condition already known unchanged.

proposed_fix.summary: Add a small decider-curated watch file, monitor/decisions/known-monitoring-conditions.json, holding fingerprints of closed monitoring-only conditions. Integrity, which has already fetched the dome page in section 5b, re-derives each entry's condition-state string from the live page and compares hashes: match -> emit finding with tracked_under=<original closed ISS> and monitoring_condition:'unchanged' (info-level in summary; decider appends a monitoring_reconfirmations[] row to the ORIGINAL closed ISS record instead of minting a new ISS — no analyst round-trip, since integrity's own fetch IS the reconfirmation); hash mismatch at same location -> emit at original severity with monitoring_condition:'changed' (the real signal, e.g. author finally splits WIN-062B) and normal ISS creation. Entries may carry optional review_after; past that date the condition re-enters normal flow once, and the decider refreshes the date on reconfirm.

content.description: Adjudicated monitoring-only conditions. Integrity 5b re-derives state_string from the live dome page per state_recipe and compares sha256. Writers: decider only (clone-and-push). See PROP-143.

state_recipe.rule: From the dome wins page, collect all element ids matching ^win-062 plus each one's data-claim-key; state_string = sorted ids joined '|' + '::' + sorted unique claim-keys joined '|'

conditions.note: Two dome entries share number WIN-062 and data-claim-key win-062-tesla-wave-speed. Our WIN-062 verdict (Misleading) covers the claim regardless of dome-side numbering. Watch is for an author-side split into WIN-062B.

files_to_modify.find: For every finding (any severity), before emitting it, search `monitor/decisions/open-issues.json` for an existing ISS that matches this finding by `category` + `location` (or close textual match). If matched, set `tracked_under: "ISS-NNN"` on the finding.
files_to_modify.replace: For every finding (any severity), before emitting it, FIRST check `monitor/decisions/known-monitoring-conditions.json` (PROP-143): if the finding's location+category match an entry, re-derive the entry's state_string from the live page per its state_recipe and compare sha256. On hash MATCH with review_after not yet passed: set `tracked_under: <entry.first_iss>` AND `monitoring_condition: "unchanged"` (downgrade to info in the human summary; the fetch you just did IS the reconfirmation). On hash MISMATCH: emit at original severity with `monitoring_condition: "changed"` and `monitoring_condition_key: <entry.key>` — this is a genuine state change (e.g. WIN-062B split) and takes the normal untracked path. On review_after passed: emit normally with `monitoring_condition: "review-due"`. THEN, for findings not matched above, search `monitor/decisions/open-issues.json` for an existing ISS that matches this finding by `category` + `location` (or close textual match). If matched, set `tracked_under: "ISS-NNN"` on the finding.

application_notes: Decider close-path addition (also at apply time, in decider prompt or decider-reporting.md): when closing an ISS as monitoring-only (fixed_by=exp-chain-endpoint + monitoring_note present), decider MAY add a known-monitoring-conditions entry using state inputs from the analyst's monitoring_note; keep entries rare and operator-reviewable (expected steady state 1-5 entries). Compute the seed entry's state_sha256 at apply time (sha256 of the state_string literal). WIN-057/057b + WIN-058/058b precedents may be candidate entries later — do NOT seed them in this PROP; only WIN-062 has two completed round-trips of evidence.
tradeoffs: Gain: eliminates a repeating ~5-touch pipeline cycle per recurrence; converts reconfirmation into a zero-marginal-cost side effect of integrity's existing page fetch; makes real author-side changes MORE visible (hash mismatch escalates at original severity with an explicit changed flag). Risk: a badly-chosen state_recipe could mask a real change -> mitigated by recipe living in the entry (reviewable), hash-mismatch fail-open to normal flow, and review_after forcing periodic full-cycle re-verification. Cost: one more small cross-agent file surface + the triple-registration burden it carries.
estimated_impact: Per suppressed recurrence: -1 ISS, -1 tracker item, -1 analyst-baby run, -2 decider touches (~1 full Sonnet run + associated Opus routing tokens). WIN-062 alone has recurred 2x in 15 days; integrity re-flags on each dome-page change while the condition persists, so expected savings recur indefinitely until the author fixes his page.
